chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah, from 'Ammar al-Sabati, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Al-istibra' (verification of pregnancy/status) is obligatory upon the one who wishes to sell the slave-girl, if he intends to have sexual relations with her, and upon the one who buys her, al-istibra' is also obligatory. I asked him: 'Is it permissible for him to have relations with her in what is other than the vagina?' He said: 'Yes, before he verifies her status. And that which indicates that abstaining from that is better.'

key_terms.الِاسْتِبْرَاءُ: Istibra: Verification of pregnancy or status of a female slave
key_terms.يَطَؤُهَا: To have sexual relations with her

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling of Istibra for a slave-girl in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahani's al-Istibsar clarifies the fiqh of 'istibra' (verification of lineage) for a pregnant slave-girl, establishing it as obligatory for both seller and buyer to ensure the child's lineage is not disputed. It permits non-vaginal intimacy before the verification period concludes, reflecting the practical flexibility in marital relations with concubines, while noting that full abstinence is spiritually superior. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on lineage purity and the distinct legal status of 'um al-walad' (mother of the child) in inheritance and manumission contexts.
